title: Stock-Split Watch: Is Nvidia Next?
content: Nvidia, the largest company by market cap, has seen its stock price rise 32% year to date and 1,479% in the past five years. Given its history of stock splits, investors are wondering if another one is on the horizon. Forward stock splits can bring down the share price and increase the number of shares outstanding, making shares more attainable to investors. Nvidia has conducted six previous stock splits, with the latest in 2024, and has seen its stock soar after each split. A reverse stock split, on the other hand, raises the stock price and lowers the share count, often used by companies at risk of not meeting exchange requirements. Nvidia's management may want to make the stock feel attainable for all investors, from large hedge funds to small retail investors.

title: Stock market holiday 2025: Are BSE, NSE open or closed on August 27 on Ganesh Chaturthi? - BusinessToday
content: Indian stock markets will be closed on Wednesday, August 27 2025, for Ganesh Chaturthi. All equity, equity‑derivatives and securities‑lending‑borrowing segments will halt; commodities will trade only in an evening session from 5 pm. The holiday is the 9th of 2025, bringing the year’s total to 14 trading holidays. The next market closures are October 2 (Mahatma Gandhi Jayanti/Dussehra), October 21–22 (Diwali), November 6 (Guru Nanak Dev) and December 25 (Christmas). On Tuesday, the BSE Sensex fell 1.04 % to 80,786.54 and the NSE Nifty50 dropped 1.02 % to 24,712.05. Technical analysts Rupak De and Sudeep Shah warned that the Nifty may stay below 24,850 and could fall toward 24,150, while the Nifty Bank may test 54,000 and 53,500, with a resistance zone at 54,900‑55,000.

title: Ganesh Chaturthi 2025: Is the stock market open or shut on August 27? Check BSE, NSE holidays
content: Dalal Street will have only four trading days in the last week of August 2025 because the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) will be closed on Wednesday, August 27 for Ganesh Chaturthi. The closure will suspend trading across equities, equity derivatives, securities lending and borrowing (SLB), currency derivatives, and electronic gold receipts (EGR). The commodities exchange MCX will also shut on that day, with no trade settlement. The week will also include a holiday on Saturday, August 30, and Sunday, August 31, reducing the week to four sessions. The next market holidays are October 2 (Gandhi Jayanti), October 21‑22 (Diwali) with a special one‑hour muhurat session on October 21, November 5 (Prakash Gurpurab), and December 25 (Christmas). Regular trading runs Monday‑Friday from 9:15 AM to 3:30 PM, preceded by a pre‑open from 9:00 AM to 9:08 AM. Block‑deal windows are at 8:45‑9:00 AM and 2:05‑2:20 PM; the closing session is 3:40‑4:00 PM. Evidence: 'Both the NSE and BSE will remain closed on Wednesday, August 27, on account of Ganesh Chaturthi.'; 'The commodities exchange, MCX will also remain shut for Ganesh Chaturthi on August 27.'; 'Regular sessions will resume on Thursday, August 28.'; 'Trading on Indian stock exchanges takes place from Monday to Friday, while markets remain closed on Saturdays, Sundays, and pre‑declared holidays.'

title: 2026年股市將崩盤？「這張圖」超神準預言...小童：網路泡沫、金融海嘯、2020年疫情大跌全抓到 | 聯合新聞網
content: An analyst on UDN discusses a century‑old cycle diagram (Bennett cycle) that supposedly predicts market highs and lows. The diagram shows 11‑year cycles for corn and pork, 11‑year highs for cotton, and a 27‑year cycle for iron with highs every 8‑10 years and lows every 7‑9‑11 years. The author claims the diagram, updated to 2059, marked ABC points where 'A表示空頭的開始', 'B表示是高價賣出的時機', and 'C表示跌深後的多頭反轉'. He cites that the diagram captured major downturns of the past decade, including the 2020 pandemic crash and the 2023 sell‑off, and that the next predicted sell point falls in 2026. The piece also references a “red‑green‑light” indicator that, according to him, has not yet turned red since April, implying the current bullish trend continues. The author warns that if the red‑green indicator turns red or the cycle shows a bearish reversal, investors should be cautious. He frames these observations as evidence that the market is near a high and may reverse soon.

title: Gogoro (GGR) Implements 1-for-20 Reverse Stock Split
content: Gogoro Inc. (NASDAQ: GGR) announced a 1‑for‑20 reverse stock split that will take effect on October 6, 2025. The split is intended to raise the share price and keep the company compliant with Nasdaq’s listing rules, while the ticker symbol GGR will stay the same and a new CUSIP number will be issued. Analysts project a potential upside of 54.33 % for the stock based on a one‑year average target price of $0.50 versus the current trading price of $0.32. GuruFocus estimates a much larger upside of 329.03 % with a projected GF Value of $1.39 for the next year, compared with the current price of $0.32399. The brokerage consensus is a ‘Hold’ rating, scored 3.0 on a 1‑to‑5 scale where 1 = Strong Buy and 5 = Sell. The company’s public warrants will remain unchanged, but their exercise price will adjust to $230 per share.
